PRENATAL GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic Fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Reason for Referral: Prenatal testing for common chromosomal trisomies
Gestational Age at Sampling: [redacted] weeks
Clinician: Dr. [redacted name]

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence-Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured amniocytes using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers specific to chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. The following markers were analyzed:

Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S390, D18S386
Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1412, D21S1414

PCR products were analyzed by capillary electrophoresis on an ABI 3500 Genetic Analyzer. Peak area ratios were calculated for informative markers.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13: Normal diallelic pattern observed
- D13S631: 1.05 (normal range 0.8-1.4)
- D13S258: 1.12 (normal range 0.8-1.4)
- D13S742: Uninformative (homozygous)
- D13S628: 0.98 (normal range 0.8-1.4)

Chromosome 18: Normal diallelic pattern observed
- D18S535: 1.08 (normal range 0.8-1.4)
- D18S391: 0.95 (normal range 0.8-1.4)
- D18S390: 1.14 (normal range 0.8-1.4)
- D18S386: Uninformative (homozygous)

Chromosome 21: Normal diallelic pattern observed
- D21S1435: 1.02 (normal range 0.8-1.4)
- D21S1411: 0.91 (normal range 0.8-1.4)
- D21S1412: 1.09 (normal range 0.8-1.4)
- D21S1414: 1.11 (normal range 0.8-1.4)

CONCLUSION
Results are consistent with a normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. No abnormality detected.

INTERPRETATION
The QF-PCR analysis shows normal biallelic patterns for all informative markers on chromosomes 13, 18, and 21, indicating the absence of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), and trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) in this fetal sample.

LIMITATIONS
1. This test is designed to detect complete trisomies of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be detected.
2. Structural chromosome abnormalities, segmental imbalances, and other chromosomal aneuploidies are not detected by this method.
3. This test does not exclude all genetic conditions or birth defects.
4. Maternal cell contamination, if present, may affect results.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Based on these normal QF-PCR results, no further chromosome analysis is required on this sample for the indication of common trisomy screening. If there are ongoing clinical concerns or ultrasound abnormalities, additional genetic testing such as chromosomal microarray or karyotyping may be considered.

Authorized by: Dr. [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Scientist
Date: [redacted date]
